proofs.text: Write a spec whose proof carries `@env(windows)`, run `--gate strong` and verify `windows-latest` is in the workflow and in the output; write a spec with no such tag and verify the workflow carries `ubuntu-latest` and not `windows-latest`; verify the workflow contains `v` followed by the `VERSION` file's contents

rule_text: The workflow carries one job per operating system the `@env` tags in `specs/` name, one linux job when they name none, and the Purlin release pinned as `v<version>`

tests.body:
def test_no_env_tag_means_one_linux_job(self, project):
        project.spec()
        project.run('--gate', 'strong')
        workflow = read(project.path('.github/workflows/purlin.yml'))
        assert 'ubuntu-latest' in workflow
        assert 'windows-latest' not in workflow
tests.name: test_no_env_tag_means_one_linux_job

def test_the_matrix_is_rendered_from_the_env_tags(self, project):
        write(project.path('specs/core/login.md'),
              SPEC.replace('@unit', '@unit @env(windows)'))
        output = project.run('--gate', 'strong')
        workflow = read(project.path('.github/workflows/purlin.yml'))
        assert 'windows-latest' in workflow
        assert 'windows-latest' in output
tests.name: test_the_matrix_is_rendered_from_the_env_tags

def test_the_purlin_release_is_pinned(self, project):
        project.run('--gate', 'strong')
        version = read(os.path.join(ROOT, 'VERSION')).strip()
        assert 'v%s' % version in read(
            project.path('.github/workflows/purlin.yml'))
tests.name: test_the_purlin_release_is_pinned
